title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a formal decision regarding a key policy or initiative, outlining its stance and intended direction. This decision aims to guide future AI development and deployment within the organization, ensuring alignment with ethical and regulatory standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The document announces a vacancy for technology specialists in AI, outlining the required qualifications and responsibilities for the role. It invites qualified candidates to apply, emphasizing the importance of AI expertise within the organization.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: This policy announces a vacancy for the position of Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office, outlining the role’s duties and the expectations for candidates. It invites qualified individuals to apply and provides contact details for submission.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This policy document outlines the opening of a new position for a Legal Officer within the AI Office. It details the duties, qualifications, and responsibilities the officer will have regarding legal oversight and compliance of AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy outlines the process for filling vacancies within the AI office, specifically targeting the role of Policy Officers. It provides guidelines for recruitment, responsibilities, and expectations for those who will manage AI-related policy matters.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with reviewing and providing scientific and technical guidance on the proposed AI Act. They evaluate the policy’s implications, assess risks, and recommend evidence-based adjustments to help shape effective, responsible AI regulation.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The draft outlines a proposal to create standard guidelines for AI development and deployment. It urges industry stakeholders to collaborate on setting clear benchmarks for safety, transparency, and accountability in AI systems.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces a consultation period for the Community of Practice (CoP) to gather input on an upcoming policy. It invites members to share their feedback and participate in shaping the policy before it is finalized.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document announces a call for people to express interest in joining a Community of Practice. It invites participants to get involved and share their expertise to help shape the community’s goals.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The policy presents a visual overview of the iterative drafting process used by the Community of Practice. It illustrates how drafts are repeatedly reviewed, revised, and refined through successive cycles to reach a polished final version.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document presents a visual timeline charting the drafting process of the Community of Practice, showing when each stage and key milestone occurred. It serves as a quick reference for stakeholders to track how the policy evolved from initial drafting through finalization.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document presents the first draft of a Code of Practice, establishing preliminary standards and guidelines for the responsible use of AI. It invites stakeholders to review and provide feedback, laying the groundwork for future refinement and wider adoption.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document presents the second draft of a Code of Practice, offering a set of updated guidelines for the ethical and responsible development and use of AI technologies. It outlines core principles such as transparency, fairness, accountability, and privacy, and gives practical recommendations for organizations to integrate these standards into their AI systems.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document outlines a set of guidelines and principles intended to ensure the responsible design, development, and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It builds on previous iterations, refining standards for safety, transparency, fairness, and accountability to support ethical AI practices.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft outlines a collaborative framework for developing and governing artificial intelligence, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and accountability. It proposes shared responsibilities and safeguards to ensure that AI benefits society while minimizing risks.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a comprehensive agreement that outlines shared principles and responsibilities for the safe and responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. It establishes guidelines for transparency, accountability, and collaboration among governments, industry, and civil society to promote trustworthy AI systems that benefit society.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: These guidelines identify specific AI practices that are forbidden, such as creating systems that can deceive or manipulate people, or that could cause physical harm or legal violations. They give developers clear rules to follow so that AI is built and used responsibly, avoiding dangerous or unethical applications.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This document explains how to identify and describe an AI system, outlining the key features and components that qualify a system as AI. It offers clear criteria and practical examples to help organizations consistently define and document their AI solutions.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies to improve communication that will help start‑ups grow and spur innovation. It encourages open, collaborative exchanges, sharing resources, expertise and networking opportunities to boost entrepreneurial success.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is an EU program that provides high-performance computing resources and support to early-stage companies. It aims to accelerate innovation by giving startups access to cutting‑edge infrastructure and expertise.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar’s slideshow covers key concepts and strategies for managing risks associated with AI and other technologies. It provides practical guidance on identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential threats in organizational settings.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar video covers risk management in the context of AI development and deployment. It discusses how to identify, evaluate, and mitigate potential risks associated with AI technologies.
